messianic_prophecies.description: Prophecies narrowing the physical and legal line of the Messiah from humanity to a specific royal family.

entries.description: The first prophecy (Protoevangelium) stating the Messiah would be born of human offspring to defeat the serpent.
The line is preserved through Adam's third son, Seth, after the death of Abel.
Noah prophesies that the Lord, the God of Shem, will dwell in his tents.
God promises that through Abraham's 'seed,' all nations of the earth will be blessed.
The covenant is specifically promised through Isaac, not Ishmael.
The 'Star out of Jacob' narrows the line to the son of Isaac over his brother Esau.
The 'Scepter' and ruler's staff are promised to remain with the tribe of Judah until 'Shiloh' comes.
The Messiah is described as a 'Shoot' or 'Branch' from the stump of Jesse (David's father).
The most specific lineage prophecy: the Messiah must be a physical heir to King David's eternal throne.
The 'signet ring' promise to Zerubbabel continues the Davidic line after the Babylonian exile.

messianic_prophecies.description: Prophecies detailing the miraculous arrival, specific locations, and events following the Messiah's birth.

entries.description: The Lord would give a sign: a virgin would conceive and bear a son called Immanuel (God with us).
Though small among the clans of Judah, Bethlehem would produce the ruler of Israel whose origins are from of old.
A 'Star' would come out of Jacob to signify the arrival of the King.
Kings from distant shores would bring tribute and present him with gifts.
A voice heard in Ramah, weeping for children who are no more, fulfilled by Herod's attempt to kill Jesus.

entries.event: Flight to and Return from Egypt
entries.description: God would call His son out of Egypt, fulfilled when the family fled Herod's persecution.
A voice in the wilderness would prepare the way for the Lord (fulfilled by John the Baptist).

entries.event: He Would be Called a Nazarene
entries.description: Prophets foretold he would be called a Nazarene, potentially a play on the Hebrew word for 'Branch' (Netzer).

messianic_prophecies.description: Prophecies detailing the Messiah's public service, miracles, and methods of teaching.

entries.description: A messenger would prepare the way before the Lord arrives at His temple.
The Spirit of the Lord would rest upon him to preach good news to the poor.
Light would dawn on the land of Zebulun and Naphtali (Galilee), a region traditionally overlooked.
The eyes of the blind would be opened, the ears of the deaf unstopped, and the lame would leap.
He would speak in parables and utter things hidden since the creation of the world.
God would raise up a prophet from among the Israelites whom the people must listen to.
The Messiah would be a light to the Gentiles and a banner for all nations.
The Lord would suddenly come to His temple to purify it.
Consumption by zeal for the Father’s house would characterize his ministry.

messianic_prophecies.description: Prophecies detailing the Messiah's betrayal, trial, physical suffering, and specific circumstances of his execution.

entries.description: The King would come to Jerusalem righteous and victorious, lowly and riding on a donkey.
Even a close friend, whom the Messiah trusted and shared bread with, would turn against him.
The exact price paid to the betrayer was foretold centuries in advance.
The betrayal money would be thrown into the house of the Lord and used to buy a potter’s field.
Like a lamb to the slaughter, he would not open his mouth to defend himself during his trial.
He would offer his back to those who beat him and his cheeks to those who pulled out his beard.
A description of death by piercing, written long before crucifixion was a common Roman practice.
Soldiers would divide his garments among them and cast lots for his seamless undergarment.
During his thirst on the cross, he was offered vinegar mixed with gall.
While soldiers typically broke the legs of the crucified to hasten death, the Messiah’s bones remained intact.
Though he died with criminals, he was assigned a grave with the rich (the tomb of Joseph of Arimathea).

messianic_prophecies.description: Prophecies concerning the Messiah's victory over the grave, his ascension, and his eventual return to establish an eternal kingdom.

entries.description: God would not leave His Holy One in the grave (Sheol) or allow his body to see decay.

entries.event: Ascension to the Right Hand of God
entries.description: The Lord said to the Messiah: 'Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool.'
He would ascend to the heights, leading a parade of captives in his wake.
The Son of Man comes with the clouds of heaven to receive an everlasting dominion and kingdom.
The Messiah (Davidic King) will gather the children of Israel and reign over them in their own land.
He will judge between nations; they will beat swords into plowshares and never train for war again.
God has sworn that every knee will bow and every tongue will acknowledge his authority.
The 'Sun of Righteousness' will rise with healing in his wings for those who revere his name.
